flags: The factorial arguments 11, 10, 9 are nonnegative integers, and 9!is nonzero.

question: What is the value of \(\dfrac{11!-10!}{9!}?\)
solution:
For a positive integer \(n\), \(n!\) is the product \(1\cdot2\cdots n\). Since the denominator is \(9!\), expand only far enough to expose that common factor:
\[
11!=11\cdot10\cdot9!,\qquad 10!=10\cdot9!.
\]
Because \(9!>0\), it can be canceled:
\[
\frac{11!-10!}{9!}
=\frac{(11\cdot10-10)9!}{9!}
=110-10=100.
\]
The value is \(\boxed{100}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
